title: Postcoital Bleeding
hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with postcoital (after intercourse) vaginal bleeding, intermenstrual bleeding, and possibly malodorous discharge. Speculum exam reveals a friable, exophytic, or ulcerated cervical lesion. Cervical cancer is the most common GYN cancer worldwide — SCC most common. Caused by persistent high-risk HPV infection (16, 18 most common). Risk factors: multiple sexual partners, early sexual activity, immunosuppression, smoking, lack of Pap screening. Diagnosis: cervical biopsy (colposcopy-directed). Staging: clinical (FIGO). Treatment: early stage (IA-IB1) → radical hysterectomy or fertility-sparing cone biopsy. Locally advanced (IB2-IVA) → chemoradiation. Metastatic → systemic therapy. Prevention: HPV vaccination, routine Pap/HPV co-testing.
